title: Catalyst — Watch the Control Loop Live

list.name: node
list.label: node
list.description: Filters EVENT panels on host_name and the daemon-LOG panels on catalyst_node_name. 'All' = .* (keeps every event, incl. the ~16% with empty host_name plus historical FQDN-alias hosts). A specific node matches the canonical short name EXACTLY (Loki anchors pipeline label-matchers), so it will MISS that node's historical FQDN aliases (e.g. RyansMini250233.rozich) and empty-host events — exactly the gap CTL-1291 asks to fix. Use All for complete history.

list.name: ev
list.label: event filter
list.description: Substring filter for the raw event-log tail and the volume panels — matches on the event name (the log body); plain text only, no regex/backslashes. Empty = all events. Examples: recovery. · phase.dispatch. · linear. · github.pr · session.heartbeat

panels.title: ▶ Watch the loop — is it thinking right now?
Recovery ticks (range)
panels.description: Per-tick evaluation summary events (recovery.tick, CTL-1287). NOTE: this event name is not currently emitted to Loki anywhere (verified over 14d) — it lights up when the delegate recovery pass runs in enforce mode. Reads 0 until then. See glossary.

panels.title: Recovery decisions (range)
panels.description: Per-item classification events (recovery.decision, CTL-1287). Not currently emitted to Loki (verified over 14d) — lights up in enforce mode. Reads 0 until then. See glossary.

panels.title: Fixes (range)
panels.description: recovery.fixed — the delegate autonomously repaired a flagged item.

panels.title: Escalations (range)
panels.description: recovery.escalated — the delegate handed an item to a human (WARN). Also drawn as red annotations on the timelines.

panels.title: Would-fix (shadow)
panels.description: recovery.would-fix — shadow-mode diagnostic: what the delegate WOULD have fixed if it were enforcing. The dominant recovery signal today.

panels.title: Dispatches launched (range)
panels.description: phase.dispatch.launched — workers the scheduler actually started this window. Proof the dispatch cycle is moving work.

panels.title: ① Tick timeline — watch the ticks (Tier 1)
Recovery pass activity by type
panels.description: Per-interval count of each recovery.* event the delegate emits (would-fix / fixed / escalated, and tick/decision once enforce mode ships). This is the live 'the recovery loop is evaluating and acting' signal. Recovery events are sparse — widen the time range if empty.

panels.title: Recovery ticks by node (enforce mode)
panels.description: recovery.tick per node — each scheduler tick the delegate evaluated flagged work. NOT EMITTED TODAY (verified 14d): populates only when the recovery pass runs in enforce mode (rMode != off AND rItems > 0). Empty is expected until then; see glossary and CTL-1291.

panels.title: Scheduler ticks by node — loop heartbeat
panels.description: phase.scheduler.* sampling events per node (parallelism-sampled + autotune-gauge). Proves the control loop itself is ticking on each node even when the recovery delegate is idle. High-volume, always-on liveness.

panels.title: ② Decisions, outcomes & the raw event stream (Tier 2)
Recovery decision & outcome stream
panels.description: Every recovery.* lifecycle event (decision/would-fix/fixed/escalated), newest first, showing node · ticket · fix_class · action. Expand a line for all fields. NOTE: rule / decision / reason live in the event's body.payload and do NOT reach Loki (CTL-1291) — only ticket (event_label) and fix_class (recovery_fix_class) are queryable today.

targets.expr: {service_name=~"${service:pipe}"} | event_name=~`recovery\..+` | host_name=~"${node:pipe}" | line_format `[{{ if .host_name }}{{ .host_name }}{{ else }}—{{ end }}] {{ .event_name }}{{ if .event_label }} · {{ .event_label }}{{ end }}{{ if .recovery_fix_class }} · fix_class={{ .recovery_fix_class }}{{ end }}`

panels.title: Recovery outcomes by fix class (range)
panels.description: Distribution of recovery.* events by recovery_fix_class (e.g. bounded-llm) and type. fix_class is present on would-fix/fixed events; escalations carry none (shown as empty).

panels.title: Recovery outcomes by ticket (range)
panels.description: Top tickets the delegate acted on, by recovery event type. event_label is the Linear ticket key.

targets.expr: topk(25, sum by (event_label, event_name) (count_over_time({service_name=~"${service:pipe}"} | event_name=~`recovery\..+` | host_name=~"${node:pipe}" [$__range])))

panels.title: Unified event-log live tail — all catalyst.* events ($ev filters)
panels.description: The raw unified event stream landing in Loki, newest first: [node] service · event_name (label). Type in the $ev box to filter by event name (e.g. recovery. , phase.dispatch. , linear. , github.pr). This is every catalyst.* EVENT record (event_name present); daemon LOG lines are excluded.

targets.expr: {service_name=~"${service:pipe}"} | event_name=~".+" | host_name=~"${node:pipe}" |= "${ev}" | line_format `[{{ if .host_name }}{{ .host_name }}{{ else }}—{{ end }}] {{ .service_name }} · {{ .event_name }}{{ if .event_label }} ({{ .event_label }}){{ end }}`

panels.title: Event volume by type — top 25 ($ev filters)
panels.description: Per-interval volume of the busiest event names. Bounded by topk(25) to keep the high-cardinality phase.<step>.<action>.<TICKET> family well under Loki's 500-series cap at the supported 6h–14d ranges (~400 distinct series at 14d; the unbounded form trips the cap there). Very wide ranges (30d+) approach the limit.

panels.title: Event volume by service
panels.description: Per-interval event volume per catalyst.* service (low cardinality, always safe). execution-core dominates; session/agent/github/linear follow.

panels.title: ③ Dispatch cycle — slots, holds & throughput (Tier 3)
Dispatch throughput — requested vs launched
panels.description: phase.dispatch.* events by action. 'requested' = the scheduler wanted to start a worker; 'launched' = it actually did. A persistent gap (requested >> launched) is back-pressure: the scheduler wants to dispatch but can't get slots. This is the live dispatch signal until CTL-1265's dispatch.held ships.

panels.title: Scheduler sampling by action
panels.description: phase.scheduler.* events by action (parallelism-sampled, autotune-gauge). Confirms the scheduler is sampling its parallelism budget each tick. The sampled VALUES (current parallelism / slots) are not in Loki — see CTL-1291; this shows the sampling cadence.

panels.title: Back-pressure & hold signals (range)
panels.description: Counts of the signals that mean 'the loop is up but admitting no new work'. On a healthy fleet most are low. 'holding new-work dispatch' and 'triage dispatch skipped' come from the daemon LOG stream (catalyst_node_name); the others from the EVENT stream (host_name). dispatch.held is the not-yet-deployed CTL-1265 event (will read 0 until it ships).

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({service_name=~"${service:pipe}"} | log_file_name=~`.+` | catalyst_node_name=~"${node:pipe}" |= `holding new-work dispatch` [$__range])) or vector(0)
sum(count_over_time({service_name=~"${service:pipe}"} | log_file_name=~`.+` | catalyst_node_name=~"${node:pipe}" |= `triage dispatch skipped` [$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Node heartbeats by node (liveness)
panels.description: node.heartbeat per node — each node's daemon publishing its periodic liveness beat. A node that flatlines here has stopped ticking. The closest available proxy for 'which nodes are alive and dispatching'.

panels.title: Hold / dispatch-skip log signals (live)
panels.description: The raw daemon-log lines behind the back-pressure gauge: 'holding new-work dispatch' (liveness snapshot stale → admitting zero new tickets, CTL-731) and 'triage dispatch skipped — respect-assignment' (CTL-781). Daemon LOG stream — filtered by catalyst_node_name.

targets.expr: {service_name=~"${service:pipe}"} | log_file_name=~`.+` | catalyst_node_name=~"${node:pipe}" |~ `holding new-work dispatch|triage dispatch skipped` | line_format `[{{ .catalyst_node_name }}] {{ .service_name }} | {{ __line__ }}`

panels.title: How to read this dashboard — and what Loki can / can't show

options.content:
## What this dashboard is

The live **watch the control loop think** view (OTL-18): the recovery delegate's evaluations and actions, the dispatch cycle, and the raw unified event stream — all from the `catalyst.*` Loki streams shipped by `otel-forward`. Sibling **OTL-17** is the higher-level health view. Filters: **$service** (which daemons), **$node** (which host), **$ev** (substring filter for the raw tail + volume panels). Default range is **6h** so the latest sparse recovery events are in view; widen for history.

## The data-path reality (read this before trusting a number)

This dashboard is **Loki-only**, and the catalyst event path has hard limits — these are documented gaps, not bugs in the panels (tracked in **CTL-1291**):

- **Event payloads don't reach Loki.** Each event's numeric `body.payload` (recovery tick's `queueSize`/`processed`/`actions{}`, decision's `rule`/`decision`/`reason`, the scheduler's `parallelism`/`slots-in-use`) is dropped at forward time — the Loki log line is just the event name. So every panel here charts **event occurrences / rates and promoted dimensions**, never the inner values. The only queryable dimensions are `event_name`, `event_entity`, `event_action`, `event_label` (the ticket/subject), `recovery_fix_class`, `host_name`, `host_id`, `catalyst_orchestration`. There are **no catalyst application metrics in Prometheus** either, so the numerics aren't recoverable elsewhere today.
- **`recovery.tick` and `recovery.decision` are not emitted yet.** Over 14d, the only recovery events in Loki are `recovery.would-fix`, `recovery.fixed`, `recovery.escalated`. The tick/decision panels (and their stat cards) are wired correctly and will populate the moment the delegate runs in **enforce mode**; until then they read **0**. The live recovery signal today is the **Recovery pass activity** panel (would-fix/fixed/escalated).
- **`dispatch.held` (CTL-1265) is not deployed** — it reads 0. The real, live dispatch signals are **requested-vs-launched** (the gap = back-pressure) and the **'holding new-work dispatch'** daemon-log line, which is currently very active.
- **Node identity on events is non-canonical.** Events carry `host_name`, which has ~10 raw values (incl. historical FQDN aliases like `RyansMini250233.rozich`) plus a ~16% **empty** bucket; the clean `catalyst_node_name` is only on daemon **logs**. So **$node = All** uses `.*` (keeps everything, incl. empty-host and alias events). Picking a **specific** node matches the canonical short name **exactly** (Loki anchors pipeline label-matchers) — it will MISS that node's historical FQDN aliases and empty-host events, so use **All** for complete history. CTL-1291 asks to stamp a canonical node name on events to fix this. The two **(log)** signals in the back-pressure gauge and the hold-log panel filter on `catalyst_node_name` instead — that's why they split cleanly by node.

## Event vs log streams

The same `catalyst.*` `service_name` carries two record kinds. **EVENT** records have an `event_name` (this dashboard's main subject) and node = `host_name`. **LOG** records have a `log_file_name` and node = `catalyst_node_name`. Event panels use `| event_name=~".+" | host_name=~"$node"`; the two daemon-log panels use `| log_file_name=~\`.+\` | catalyst_node_name=~"$node"`.

## Why `topk` on the volume panel

`event_name` is high-cardinality (the `phase.<step>.<action>.<TICKET>` family is 2,900+ distinct names over 14d). A bare `sum by (event_name)` over a wide range trips Loki's 500-series cap and blanks the panel, so the volume-by-type panel is bounded with `topk(25, …)` (≈400 series at 14d, safely under the cap; 30d+ approaches it). Volume-by-service is low-cardinality and unbounded.

## Acceptance-criteria map (OTL-18)

- **Tier 1 — watch the ticks:** Recovery pass activity + Recovery ticks by node + Scheduler ticks (loop heartbeat).
- **Tier 2 — decisions + raw stream:** Recovery decision & outcome stream + outcomes tables + the **Unified event-log live tail** (filterable by `$ev`).
- **Tier 3 — dispatch visibility:** requested-vs-launched throughput + scheduler sampling + back-pressure/hold gauge + node heartbeats + hold-log feed.

panels.title: Scheduler slots per node — current · target · effective · running
panels.description: The autotuner's slot ceiling vs actual usage, per node, charted directly from the scheduler's own gauges (CTL-1291 promoted these to Loki structured metadata). target/effective come from phase.scheduler.autotune-gauge; current from phase.scheduler.parallelism-sampled; running_workers (actual concurrent workers = real slots in use) from autotune-gauge. When running approaches effective the node is saturated; when current/target diverge the autotuner is throttling.

panels.title: Node load & free memory per node
panels.description: Per-node scheduler load (1-min load average) and free-memory %, from phase.scheduler.parallelism-sampled structured metadata (CTL-1291). These are the headroom signals the autotuner reacts to: rising load1 / falling mem_free_pct is what pulls effective parallelism down. load1 on the left axis (short), free-memory % on the right axis (percent).
